All required suites pass. Here is the summary.

## Result
- Goal/task: G-20260805T040948887161Z-8678e914 / **T-20260805T040948888613Z-d4e830c9**
- Role: Implementer (Claude Code)
- Status: **complete** (implementation done; delivery — commit/PR/merge — is owned by the Shiki loop)

## What changed
Wired the existing `codeowners_required_owner()` resolver into all three ownership sites so a repository owned by anyone can satisfy its own CODEOWNERS check. All edits stayed within the declared locks.

- **Enforcement — `scripts/validate_shiki.py`**: `validate_codeowners_governance(root=ROOT)` now resolves `required_owner = codeowners_required_owner(root)` and checks against it. `main()` still calls it argless, so `ROOT` (the running repo, which is the target root when validate runs inside a target) is the default — platform behavior unchanged.
- **Enforcement — `scripts/shiki_doctor.py`**: `_codeowners_findings(target)` resolves the owner per target (`:426` import + `:454/:463/:464`). Constant stays the documented fallback.
- **Target write — `scripts/shiki_installer.py`**: `install_template` resolves the owner once and threads `codeowners_owner` through `copy_path`. The fresh-write path substitutes the owner into `.github/CODEOWNERS` only when `target_install and owner != constant`; otherwise it copies verbatim (no-repo.json installs are byte-identical to today). The `.new` path is left verbatim on purpose. This repo's own copy is never touched (install only writes to a target dir).
- **Fixtures — `scripts/test_shiki_doctor.sh`**: `make_target` now seeds `.shiki/repo.json` *before* `install-target` (so substitution fires); parameterized so `NO_REPO` installs with no repo.json and the fallback owner matches the shipped file. No assertion weakened.
- **Fixtures — `scripts/test_shiki_start.sh`**: added `seed_repo_json` and seeded `$TARGET` + the three retry targets before their first `start` (start validates at the end of install and keeps an existing CODEOWNERS on re-run, so an unseeded 2nd run would fail install-validate). No assertion weakened.
- **Tests**: new `tests/test_codeowners_wiring.py` (5 cases incl. the load-bearing foreign-owner target passing both `validate_codeowners_governance` **and** `doctor.codeowners.coverage`); extended `tests/test_install_force_semantics.py` with an installed foreign-owner target passing the wired gate.

## Checklist status
- Skill Gate: `tdd` (red → green: new test failed pre-wiring, passes after), `code-review` (self-review of installer/enforcement diffs) ✅
- TDD: ✅  · CCA: n/a (loop-owned) · MergeGate: n/a (loop-owned)

## Evidence (local, diagnostic)
- `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py` → **passed**
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **Ran 1019 tests, OK** (+6 new)
- `test_shiki_doctor.sh`, `test_shiki_start.sh`, `test_shiki_init.sh`, `test_shiki_control_plane.sh` → all **passed** (+ `test_shiki_shellcheck.sh` passed)
- `codeowners_required_owner()` now has production consumers in `validate_shiki.py`, `shiki_doctor.py`, `shiki_installer.py`
- `git status`: only locked files changed; `.github/CODEOWNERS` untouched

## Note (out-of-locks follow-up, not a blocker)
The installer/enforcement are consistently **repo.json-based**. There is a residual gap in `scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py` `cmd_init` (not in this task's locks): it runs `install_template` **before** `write_target_repo_config`, so a brand-new `shiki init --repo acme/x` still ships the fallback owner until repo.json exists (the fixtures seed repo.json first to exercise the wired path, which also matches any re-run since start persists repo.json). Closing that end-to-end for a fresh first-run init would need `shiki_bootstrap.py` in scope — reported as a stop rather than reached into. Recorded in memory (`codeowners-owner-wiring`).

Loop owns commit → PR (with MergeGate body) → CCA → merge.
